source.title: Objaverse-XL: A Universe of 10M+ 3D Objects
source.authors: Matt Deitke; Ruo-Shi Liu; Matthew Wallingford; Huong Ngo; Oscar Michel; Aditya Kusupati; Alan Fan; Christian Laforte; Vikram S. Voleti; S. Gadre; Eli VanderBilt; Aniruddha Kembhavi; Carl Vondrick; Georgia Gkioxari; Kiana Ehsani; Ludwig Schmidt; Ali Farhadi

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether performance improves with data scale using 3D-vision models and task metrics, rather than language-model held-out loss or the original scaling-law method.
record.gate_note: The study varies 3D training-dataset size and reports novel-view-synthesis performance, and compares PixelNeRF trained from scratch with PixelNeRF pretrained on Objaverse-XL. It does not fit or test power laws for language-model loss, parameters, tokens, or compute. The reported 3D scaling results are relevant to V6, but do not establish the power-law form required by V5.
record.test_reason: This is a 3D dataset paper. It cites Kaplan and Hoffmann as motivation and reports that novel-view-synthesis metrics improve with training-set size (Fig. 6). It fits no power law, reports no loss and works with no language models. So it cannot show the power-law form V5 requires. V6 concerns language-model downstream performance versus scale or loss, which this study does not measure. Table 3 compares pretraining on the authors' own dataset against training from scratch; it is not a scale sweep. The finding of monotone improvement with data is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that scaling 3D training data, with the model architecture held constant, shows promising empirical trends: performance improves from about 1K to 10M objects with few signs of slowing. They also find that pretraining on Objaverse-XL improves PixelNeRF after fine-tuning on DTU and ShapeNet, and that alignment fine-tuning on a high-quality subset improves Zero123-XL (Table 2). They make no power-law claim.
record.recipe_differences: This is a 3D-vision dataset-scaling study using novel-view-synthesis metrics and dataset-size sweeps, not the language-model loss, parameter/token/compute measurements, or fitting procedure of the original sources.

fits_no_version.finding: In 3D novel-view synthesis, task metrics (PSNR for PixelNeRF, LPIPS for Zero123) improve monotonically as training data grows from about 1K to 2M and from 800 to 10M objects, with architecture fixed. No power-law fit and no loss are reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task quality of 3D vision models improves monotonically with training-data size over several orders of magnitude, with no sign of saturation.

record.peer_reviewed: Neural Information Processing Systems (2023); the text also identifies the manuscript as a preprint under review.
record.problems: The dataset-size sweep results in Figure 6 are presented as plots without numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The study reports 3D task metrics, not power-law fits or language-model loss.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results left out.

untested.parts: All: no language-model loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
All: no fitted law and no extrapolation.
All: the architecture is held fixed.
Power-law form in 3D vision: no fit and no loss are reported, only monotone metric curves.
Language-model downstream performance versus scale or loss.
All: no fits, so no fit-dependence.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked all rows to V6 and labelled them supports. That is wrong: V6 concerns language models, and the study fits no power law, so V5 cannot be decided. Table 2 (alignment fine-tuning) is not a scaling result and is correctly omitted. The Zero123 sweep confounds dataset size with dataset source above 800K.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether laws fitted on small language-model runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study uses 3D models and varies training-data scale, but does not test whether a power-law form holds in this modality or in other training regimes.
The study examines 3D novel-view-synthesis metrics under dataset scaling and pretraining; it does not test downstream performance as a function of language-model pretraining loss or model size.
Dependence of fitted language-model exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup and fitting choices.

rows.subject: PixelNeRF
rows.operation_detail: Trained on varying numbers of Objaverse-XL objects and evaluated on a held-out subset of Objaverse-XL.

conditions.value: varying scales; figure shows approximately 1K to 2M

rows.note: The authors state that quality consistently improves with more objects, including at 2 million objects and 24 million rendered images. The plotted values are not reported numerically in the text.
rows.check: PixelNeRF PSNR rises with dataset size (1K to 2M) on a log x-axis, figure only. There is no fit and no loss, so the power-law form cannot be read. It is not a V6 row, since the model is not a language model.

rows.subject: Zero123
rows.operation_detail: Trained with varying dataset sizes and evaluated on a zero-shot dataset.

conditions.value: varying scales; figure spans approximately 800 to 10M, with the 800K point being Zero123 and the 10M point Zero123-XL

rows.note: The authors state that the visual-similarity score continues to improve as dataset size increases. The figure caption identifies the 800K and 10M endpoints as Zero123 and Zero123-XL, respectively; plotted values are not reported numerically in the text.
rows.check: Figure only, with no fit. The evaluation set is Google Scanned Objects (Sec. 4.1). Points below 800K are Objaverse 1.0 subsets, while the 10M point is Zero123-XL trained on Objaverse-XL, so dataset source changes with size. LPIPS is plotted ×10. It is not a V6 row.

rows.subject: PixelNeRF
rows.operation_detail: Compared training from scratch with pretraining on Objaverse-XL followed by fine-tuning.
rows.note: The table reports the pretrained model's result as 17.53 ±.37.
rows.check: Pretraining on Objaverse-XL versus training from scratch on DTU. This is a transfer benefit of the authors' own dataset, not a scale sweep or a power law. The baseline 15.32 has no reported uncertainty.

rows.subject: PixelNeRF
rows.operation_detail: Compared training from scratch with pretraining on Objaverse-XL followed by fine-tuning.
rows.note: The table reports the pretrained model's result as 24.22 ±.55.
rows.check: Same as R3, on ShapeNet (22.71 to 24.22). There is no scaling variable, so the row does not bear on any version.
